caseStudies.title: Ticker Talk: Cited Answers from SEC Filings
caseStudies.challenge: Fundamental analysts spend hours in 10-K and 10-Q filings to confirm a single figure. General-purpose chatbots answer quickly but cannot show which filing, period, and unit a number came from, and they happily use facts that were published after the date in question.
caseStudies.approach: A Next.js workspace over a FastAPI service and a background worker, with PostgreSQL as the single source of truth. The agent plans and retrieves, but deterministic code owns accounting, units, and calculations, and every answer carries citations to the exact filing. An evaluation harness computes expected answers point-in-time, so a test can never reward look-ahead.
outcomes: Answers cite the filing accession, period, unit, and as-of cutoff behind every figure
Point-in-time evaluation: 17 golden questions scored by a deterministic scorer plus a pinned LLM judge
Missing or restated data surfaces as an explicit gap instead of a zero or a partial period
Released only through a gate of real browser journeys against staging and production

caseStudies.title: Knowledge Graph for a Global HealthTech Support Knowledge Base
caseStudies.challenge: A global healthtech company had tens of thousands of Salesforce knowledge base articles across their product portfolio. Content was outdated, duplicated, and impossible to query across product domains. Manual quality audits could not scale.
caseStudies.approach: Built an ingestion pipeline from Salesforce exports into a knowledge graph on Azure Cosmos DB (Gremlin API), after prototyping on Neo4j, with a FAISS index for semantic retrieval. Every article gets an automated quality scorecard. Editors work in a React app with a Sigma.js graph explorer and a tool-calling chat agent that queries the graph and the vector index.
outcomes: Per-article quality scorecard: completeness, structure, staleness, duplicates, translation coverage, broken links, contradictions
Tool-calling chat agent (Semantic Kernel, Azure OpenAI) over the graph and the vector index
Batched graph writes cut vertex upsert time 7.8x (11.6s to 1.5s per 10 items)
Request-unit budgets, Prometheus metrics, and Grafana dashboards for every ingestion stage

caseStudies.title: Network Anomaly Detection PoC for a Major European Telecom
caseStudies.challenge: The operator's network operations team was working through alerts from siloed monitoring systems. Dashboards could not correlate events across fiber-to-the-home network layers or suggest a root cause, so incident resolution was slow.
caseStudies.approach: A three-stage agent pipeline (Sense, Think, Act) over FTTH network telemetry, driven by Celery and RabbitMQ, with results in MongoDB. The Act stage uses LLM tool calling to reboot a device, reset its configuration, or open a Jira ticket. Operators see results in Grafana and question them in Open WebUI, and their feedback drives a prompt-revision loop.
outcomes: Sense, Think, and Act agents with tool calls for ONU reboots, config resets, and Jira tickets
Grafana dashboards for anomalies, incidents, and agent activity, with drill-down to individual runs
Open WebUI chat grounded in incident records for plain-language investigation
Feedback loop that drafts a revised agent prompt when more than 30% of recent outputs are rated bad
caseStudies.screenshotCaption: Incidents written by the agents, from a local re-run of the proof of concept on synthetic telemetry. Ticket links are blurred.

caseStudies.title: Multi-Brand Headless Storefront for a Global FMCG
caseStudies.challenge: A global FMCG company needed a next-generation headless storefront to serve two premium consumer brands from a single codebase. The existing Magento 2 monolith made launching a second brand a 9-month effort, and the frontend was too slow for modern commerce expectations.
caseStudies.approach: Co-architected a GraphCommerce-based PWA with Next.js, a GraphQL BFF layer stitching Magento and Hygraph CMS, and a design token architecture enabling rapid brand switching. Built CI/CD with blue/green zero-downtime deployments on Azure.
outcomes: Headless PWA serving two premium brands from one Next.js codebase
Second-brand onboarding reduced from 9 months to 2 months (78% faster)
Release cycle time cut 30% with blue/green zero-downtime CI/CD
6 engineers mentored across design, QA, and product
